experiment: BMS-626529 molecular docking into gp120 relay pocket

relay_pocket_docking.interpretation: BMS-626529 binds the relay pocket with -6.7 kcal/mol, exceeding the standard druggability threshold of -6.0 kcal/mol. The 2.15 kcal/mol gap between mode 1 and mode 2 suggests a single dominant binding pose with good specificity.

fostemsavir_site_control.note: Lower affinity at the attachment site is expected: 6MEO captures the post-CD4 conformation where the attachment site has already engaged CD4. BMS-626529 is designed to bind the pre-CD4 conformation (PDB 5U7O). The control confirms that the relay pocket affinity is not an artifact of the scoring function.

comparative_analysis.significance: BMS-626529 shows 1.5 kcal/mol stronger binding at the relay pocket than at its own therapeutic target in the same structure. This provides independent computational evidence that the relay pocket is druggable.
